findings.what: The delivery mints a brand-new top-level i18n namespace `ClientIdentifiers` for H-20's client-own-identifiers copy, directly contradicting the brief's binding text (repeated twice: "Orchestrator decisions" and §5 Web slice): "extend `ClientKnowledge` ... and `ArApCounterparty` ... no third namespace" / "do not mint a third namespace (shared file — keep the edit localised)". `en.json` is a wave-shared file (WORK-ORDER rule 8, brief risk 13) precisely because multiple concurrent tickets edit it; adding a new top-level key instead of nesting under `ArApCounterparty` is exactly the kind of non-localised edit the rule exists to prevent. The final report's own "Docs updated" and "Assumptions" sections do not mention or justify this deviation.
findings.evidence: git diff origin/main...HEAD -- apps/web/messages/en.json shows `+  "ClientIdentifiers": { "heading": ..., "addTrigger": "Add identifier", ... }` as a new top-level object (sibling of `ArApCounterparty`, not nested inside it). Two call sites use `useTranslations("ClientIdentifiers")`. No test hardcodes the namespace name (they assert rendered strings), so the fix is contained.
findings.fix: Move the `ClientIdentifiers` block's keys under `ArApCounterparty.clientIdentifiers` (or another existing namespace's sub-object), update the two `useTranslations("ClientIdentifiers")` call sites to `useTranslations("ArApCounterparty.clientIdentifiers")`, and re-run `client-identity-section.test.tsx` / the Playwright walk to confirm the rendered strings are unchanged.

findings.what: AC6's own text (gh issue #647, and gap-647.md/brief-647.md's TDD seam (e)) explicitly requires verifying "meaningful loading" and "partial/stale" as journey states, alongside empty/filtered/invalid-saving/denied/cancelled-recovery. Every other named state (empty, filtered-to-nothing, denied 403, invalid/saving via the confirm-gate and CLR23 refusal, cancelled+recovery, 320px, 200% zoom, keyboard/focus, reduced motion, stable URL/Back, preserved draft) has a dedicated cell across the Playwright walk and/or the three jsdom files. "loading" and "partial/stale" have none — no cell asserts a loading skeleton/spinner state is reached, and none exercises a partial failure (e.g. one of `ClientIdentitySection`'s three independent `useAsyncRead`s — identities/corrections/identifiers — failing or returning stale data while the others succeed). The final report marks AC6 "done" with no residual named for either state.
findings.evidence: `grep -n "stale\|Skeleton\|loading\|Loading" apps/web/e2e/counterparty-identity-walk.spec.ts apps/web/components/registers/counterparty-identity-panel.test.tsx apps/web/components/registers/client-identity-section.test.tsx apps/web/components/registers/counterparty-identity-correct.test.tsx` returns nothing; `counterparty-identity-mock.mjs` fixtures are `clientOk / clientEmpty / clientDenied / clientVendorOnly` only, no delayed/partial-failure fixture. The 17 Playwright test titles (grep `^test(`) list every other required state by name but never "loading" or "stale"/"partial".
findings.fix: Add at least one cell exercising the loading state (e.g. delay the mock's `get_counterparty_identity`/`list_counterparty_identity` response and assert the loading affordance renders before data), and one exercising a partial/stale read (e.g. have `list_counterparty_merge_corrections` 500 while `list_counterparty_identity`/`loadClientIdentifiers` succeed, and assert the section shows the succeeded halves plus a scoped error for the failed one, per `ClientIdentitySection`'s three-independent-reads design). If genuinely deferred, name it as a residual in the final report rather than marking AC6 done outright.

findings.where: apps/web/components/registers/counterparty-identity-panel.tsx:10-19 (header comment) and its use of components/registers/knowledge-shared.tsx
findings.what: The brief's "Surface ownership" section names five `knowledge-shared.tsx` exports to "call verbatim": `KnowledgeSourceBlock`, `knowledgeValueText`, `appliesWhenText`, `KnowledgeKindBadge`, `KnowledgeTrustBadge`. Only `KnowledgeSourceBlock` is used; the other four are never imported or called anywhere in the delivered diff. The deviation is defensible on inspection — `KnowledgeKindBadge`'s translations (`ClientKnowledge.kind.*` = assertion/extracted_fact/preference/policy) and `KnowledgeTrustBadge`'s (`ClientKnowledge.trust.*` = asserted/extracted/imported_unverified/inferred) have no counterpart in the counterparty-identity domain (kind=vendor/customer; there is no "trust" concept on an alias at all in migration 0200), so calling them as directed would either mis-render or require inventing data the schema does not carry — but the final report's "Assumptions" section is silent on this specific deviation (it explains why the `KnowledgeBadges`/`KnowledgeApplicability`/`KnowledgeProvenance` record-typed wrappers are not called, but not why the four atomic "call verbatim" functions are also unused).
findings.evidence: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- apps/web | grep -n 'knowledgeValueText\|appliesWhenText\|KnowledgeKindBadge\|KnowledgeTrustBadge'` returns nothing. `apps/web/components/registers/knowledge-shared.tsx:47-73` shows `KnowledgeKindBadge`/`KnowledgeTrustBadge` keyed to `ClientKnowledge.kind.*`/`ClientKnowledge.trust.*`, whose only values (checked via en.json) are assertion/extracted_fact/preference/policy and asserted/extracted/imported_unverified/inferred — none matching vendor/customer or human_ui/agent/seeding/legacy_unknown.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the final report's Assumptions naming this deviation and the domain-vocabulary mismatch that justifies it, so a reviewer does not have to re-derive it from the code comments.
